title: The Erdős–Lovász cover number problem: g(6) = 17, and new lower bounds for every r
description:
The Erdős–Lovász cover number problem, posed in 1974 in the paper that introduced the local lemma, asks for the minimum number of edges g(r) in an r-uniform intersecting hypergraph with cover number r. The exact values known before this work are g(3) = 6, g(4) = 9 and g(5) = 13. For large r the best published lower bound is g(r) ≥ (3.0534… − o(1)) r (Sivashankar, arXiv:2606.24878), and Kahn showed that g(r) is linear in r.

This record contains two results.

1. The case r = 6: g(6) = 17 (Papers 1–4, computer-assisted).

A reproducible computer-assisted determination of g(6), the smallest number of blocks in a pairwise intersecting 6-uniform family whose transversal number is 6.

The lower bound is reached in two stages. Families of at most fifteen cards are excluded by two independent routes: a weighted counting inequality with thirteen degree histograms, and a stronger eleven-card lemma stating that every pairwise intersecting 6-uniform family of eleven cards has a four-element transversal. Sixteen cards are then excluded in two branches: 341 twelve-card kernels of maximum symbol degree three are enumerated and shown to admit no extension, and every other case reduces to one of 463 canonical eight-card cores; every associated CNF instance is unsatisfiable, and every unsatisfiability carries a DRAT certificate accepted by an independent proof checker. The upper bound is an explicit seventeen-card family on 27 symbols for which all 136 pairs intersect and none of the 80,730 five-symbol subsets is a transversal. Hence g(6) = 17.

2. Every r: new lower bounds (Paper 5, proposed proofs). In the framework of Sivashankar it proves:

  • that the residual cover constant +4 can be +3, answering his question, so g(r) ≥ 3r − 3 for every r (attained at r = 3 and 4);
  • g(r) ≥ 3r − 2 for every r ≥ 16, by excluding the equality case;
  • a new asymptotic lower bound, liminf g(r)/r ≥ 3 + 5(133 − 2√3185)/1414 = 3.0711…, above the constant 3.0534 of Sivashankar. The proof is deterministic: a bound on the cards deleted in the last steps of a maximum-degree peeling, a saving of peeling symbols when one cover of the remainder meets most cards of a group, a budget count on the traces of the deleted cards, and the rainbow matching theorem of Correia, Pokrovskiy and Sudakov (IMRN 2023). The constant is reached where a stability bound for large remainders meets this saving, and its algebra is checked symbolically by a script in the archive.

These proofs are unreviewed outside this project; their finite steps are checked by scripts in the archive.

The archive contains five papers and an overview, the enumeration and verification scripts, the canonical core data, the reduction data, SAT run records, the certificate summary, three representative CNF/DRAT pairs, and an independent re-verification log recording what was re-run and what remains a reading obligation.

DRAT certification removes the SAT solver from the trusted base. It does not establish that the reduction reaches every counterexample, nor that the encoding means what the mathematics means; both are named as open obligations in the text.

Status. Research draft. No priority is claimed. The lower bound is computer-assisted and has not been independently reviewed by a human referee or a proof assistant: DRAT certification removes the SAT solver from the trusted base, but the completeness of the finite reduction and the faithfulness of the CNF encoding remain open obligations that no certificate discharges. The upper bound is an explicit witness and is checkable directly. AI tools (ChatGPT, OpenAI; Claude, Anthropic) were used throughout the work and its review; every number reported is regenerated by a script or certified by a proof file in the archive.

The full certificate archive is not in this record. This deposit carries the repository only. The complete set of 463 CNF files and 463 DRAT proofs, with the per-core checker output and verification markers, is about 534 MB and is published as the release asset g6-certificates-463.zip at github.com/Osman209/g6-equals-17/releases. The three hardest instances ship inside this deposit in data/cnf/, so the certification step can be reproduced without it.
